answer: Each identity runs one forge and locks a 65-credit bond. Each epoch it draws one thread through its die and files a key-signed thread record of spool and diameter, plus its nadir spool, the lowest tensile reading. An auditor recomputes the registry and re-pulls the nadir spool; a missing record, duplicate spool, or nadir mismatch burns the bond. A fake needs a new die: first costs 34, k-th pays 34+4(k-1), 1000th pays 4030, so 1000 fakes pay 2,032,000 with 65,000 at risk. A rented-die ring fails because one die marks every thread identically. An honest forge pays 34 once and keeps its bond.
